rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named / mood lands per beat (8+/10 floor on teaching beats).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer block carries a dated accept-note (2026-08-19, Antti-directed, quoted: "human close can be a beat before actual full closing. It is deliberately there to have the time for closing conversations") that rules on exactly this reading: `## Human close` is a deliberate PRE-close beat, not the module's ending; the closer lecture chain + Key Concepts + Optional challenges + Next are meant to follow it, by design, and future judges should not re-flag. Per dispatch-preamble instruction to check for an existing accept-note before flagging a passage, this rule is scored against that ruling rather than re-derived. Two facts the note cites were independently verified this cycle, not taken on trust: (1) `grep -l '## Optional challenges' *.md` in `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/` returns SIX files — getting-going.md, earn-the-trust.md, plan-mode-done-right.md, run-the-first-experiment.md, learn-from-the-test.md, and this file — confirming Optional challenges is a repo-wide convention, not an M6-specific insertion. (2) Counting `## `-headers after each module's last teaching beat (`grep -n '^## '`): M4 (run-the-first-experiment.md) has 5 trailing sections after `## Start here` (Key Concepts, Optional challenges, Bring to Module 5, Pre-reads before Module 5, Next); M5 (learn-from-the-test.md) has 4 trailing sections after its last teaching beat `## Back to the map, one last time` (Optional challenges, Bring to Module 6, Pre-reads before Module 6, Next); M6 has 3 trailing sections after `## Human close` (Key Concepts, Optional challenges, Next) — fewer than both siblings, and 2 of the difference is definitional (no `## Bring to Module 7` / `## Pre-reads before Module 7` exist because M6 is the terminal module). The note's claim holds exactly as stated. The cached persona trace (unchanged this cycle — the maintainer-block-only edit does not touch body text; `diff` against the last-audited body confirms only wording tightening + the Optional-challenges insertion, both already reflected in the 2026-08-19 trace) still shows the opinionated-senior persona's close mood at 5/10 (down from 6/10 pre-Optional-challenges), below the mechanical 7-floor. That number is real and not disputed, but the accept-note directly engages the mechanism behind it (declared-close-then-more-content) and chooses to keep the tension on purpose, for a stated reason ("the conversation needs a named slot, and the name is what makes a trainer stop for it") — a tradeoff, not an oversight. Filing REVISE again would re-derive the same structural objection the note already ruled on without identifying anything the note failed to address; the verified counts show the design is, if anything, more disciplined than its two siblings, which undercuts the count-based half of the original harm theory. Scored PASS; the sub-7 persona score is recorded honestly below (mood_summary) as a known, accepted, non-blocking tension rather than omitted.

Close reads as recognition/competence-as-posture throughout ("I know how to test, I know how to learn, I know how to encode"); no shame-framing anywhere in body. Optional challenges bullets are opt-in stretch prompts ("Pick one when you want to"), not remediation. Unaffected by this cycle's maintainer-only edit.
